bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第138卷 卷第一百三十八 。

translations.literal: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 138, Volume 138.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 138.

sentences.zh: 【齊紀四】 昭陽作噩，一年。

translations.literal: [Qi Annals 4] Zhaoyang Zuoe; one year.
translations.idiomatic: [Qi Annals 4] The year Zhaoyang Zuoe—one year in all.

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝下永明十一年（癸酉，公元四九三年） 。

translations.literal: Under the Shizu, Emperor Wu, Yongming year 11 (Guiyou, 493 CE).
translations.idiomatic: Yongming year 11 of Emperor Wu of Qi (Guiyou, 493 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，以驃騎大將軍王敬則為司空，鎮軍大將軍陳顯達為江州刺史。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Wang Jingze was made Grand Cavalry General and Minister of Works; Chen Xianda was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Emperor Wu appointed Grand Cavalry General Wang Jingze Minister of Works and General Who Pacifies the Army Chen Xianda governor of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 顯達自以門寒位重，每遷官，常有愧懼之色，戒其子勿以富貴陵人；

translations.literal: Xianda, considering his humble birth and heavy rank, whenever he was promoted often showed a look of shame and fear, and admonished his sons not to lord wealth and rank over others;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda felt keenly that he had risen far from humble origins; each promotion brought him shame and anxiety, and he warned his sons never to flaunt wealth or rank over others;

sentences.zh: 而諸子多事豪侈，顯達聞之，不悅。

translations.literal: But his sons mostly indulged in luxury; when Xianda heard of it, he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: His sons, however, mostly lived lavishly; when Xianda learned of it, he was unhappy.

sentences.zh: 子休尚為郢府主簿，過九江。

translations.literal: His son Xiushang served as chief clerk of the Ying prefecture staff and passed through Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chen Xiushang, serving as chief clerk on the staff at Ying, traveled through Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 顯達曰：「麈尾蠅拂是王、謝家物，汝不須捉此！」

translations.literal: Xianda said: "Deer's-tail and fly-whisk fans are objects of the Wang and Xie families—you need not hold these!"
translations.idiomatic: Xianda said, "Deer's-tail and fly-whisk fans belong to the great clans Wang and Xie—you have no business handling such things!

sentences.zh: 即取於前燒之。

translations.literal: He immediately took them before him and burned them.
translations.idiomatic: He snatched them from his son's hands and burned them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 初，上於石頭造露車三千乘，欲步道取彭城。

translations.literal: Initially, the emperor had constructed three thousand open wagons at Shitou, intending to march on foot and take Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had had three thousand uncovered wagons built at Shitou, planning to take Pengcheng on foot.

sentences.zh: 魏人知之，劉昶數泣訴於魏主，乞處邊戍，招集遺民，以雪私恥。

translations.literal: When the Wei learned of it, Liu Chang wept repeatedly before the Wei emperor, begging to be posted on the frontier, to gather scattered populations, and to wipe away his private shame.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Wei learned of this, Liu Chang pleaded tearfully before the Wei emperor to serve on the frontier, rally dispersed loyalists, and redeem his disgrace.

sentences.zh: 魏主大會公卿於經武殿，以議南伐，於淮、泗間大積馬芻。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor convened the nobles and officials at the Jingwu Hall to discuss a southern campaign, and amassed great stores of fodder along the Huai and Si rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor convened dukes and officials in the Hall of Military Classics to debate invading south, while stockpiling fodder on a vast scale between the Huai and Si.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，以右衛將軍崔慧景為豫州刺史以備之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he appointed Cui Huijing Right Guards General and Governor of Yu Province to guard against it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu heard of this and appointed Right Guards General Cui Huijing governor of Yu Province to prepare defenses.

sentences.zh: 魏遣員外散騎侍郎邢巒等來聘。

translations.literal: Wei sent Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary Xing Luan and others on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei sent Xing Luan, an extraordinary attendant, and others as envoys.

sentences.zh: 巒，穎之孫也。

translations.literal: Luan was the grandson of Xing Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Luan was a grandson of Xing Shuo.

sentences.zh: 丙子，文惠太子長懋卒。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Crown Prince Wenhuiz Changmao died.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi, Crown Prince Changmao died.

sentences.zh: 太子風韻甚和，上晚年好游宴，尚書曹事分送太子省之，由是威加內外。

translations.literal: The crown prince's bearing was very harmonious; in the emperor's later years he delighted in banquets and excursions, and matters of the Masters of Writing were forwarded to the crown prince for review, whereby his authority extended inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was gentle and even-tempered; as the emperor in his later years grew fond of feasting and travel, memorials from the secretariat were routed to the crown prince for review, and his authority reached throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 太子性奢靡，治堂殿、園囿過於上宮，費以千萬計，恐上望見之，乃傍門列修竹；

translations.literal: The crown prince was by nature extravagant; the halls and gardens he built exceeded the upper palace, costing tens of millions; fearing the emperor might see them, he planted tall bamboo beside the gates;
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was extravagant by nature; the halls and gardens he built outdid the imperial palace and cost tens of millions; lest the emperor glimpse them from afar, he lined the gates with tall bamboo;

sentences.zh: 凡諸服玩，率多僭侈。

translations.literal: Of all his garments and curios, most were presumptuously lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly everything he wore or collected smacked of presumptuous luxury.

sentences.zh: 啟於東田起小苑，使東宮將吏更番築役，營城包巷，彌亙華遠。

translations.literal: He opened a small park on the Eastern Fields, set the Eastern Palace officers and clerks to rotate in construction duty, walled streets and lanes, and the splendor stretched far.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out a private park on the Eastern Fields and set Eastern Palace officers to build in rotating shifts, walling off whole blocks until the complex sprawled in lavish grandeur.

sentences.zh: 上性雖嚴，多布耳目，太子所為，人莫敢以聞。

translations.literal: Although the emperor's nature was strict, he placed many informants; no one dared report what the crown prince did.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor was strict by nature, he had informants everywhere, and no one dared report the crown prince's doings.

sentences.zh: 上嘗過太子東田，見其壯麗，大怒，收監作主帥；

translations.literal: The emperor once passed the crown prince's Eastern Fields, saw how grand they were, flew into a rage, and imprisoned the supervising commanders;
translations.idiomatic: Once, passing the crown prince's Eastern Fields, the emperor saw how grand they were, flew into a rage, and had the supervising officers arrested;

sentences.zh: 太子皆藏之，由是大被誚責。

translations.literal: The crown prince hid them all, and for this was severely rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince concealed them all and was sharply rebuked for it.

sentences.zh: 又使嬖人徐文景造輦及乘輿御物；

translations.literal: He also had his favorite Xu Wenjing make imperial carriages and regalia;
translations.idiomatic: He also had his favorite Xu Wenjing build imperial carriages and regalia;

sentences.zh: 上嘗幸東宮，匆匆不暇藏輦，文景乃以佛像內輦中，故上不疑。

translations.literal: The emperor once visited the Eastern Palace; in the hurry there was no time to hide the carriage, so Wenjing placed a Buddha image inside it, and the emperor did not suspect.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor once visited the Eastern Palace, there was no time to hide the carriage; Wenjing stuffed a Buddha image inside it, and the emperor suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 文景父陶仁謂文景曰：「我正當掃墓待喪耳！」

translations.literal: Wenjing's father Tao Ren said to Wenjing: "I ought simply to sweep graves and await the mourning!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing's father Tao Ren told him, "All I should do now is tend graves and wait for the funeral!

sentences.zh: 仍移家避之。

translations.literal: He then moved his household to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his household away to distance himself from his son.

sentences.zh: 後文景竟賜死，陶仁遂不哭。

translations.literal: Later Wenjing was indeed ordered to die; Tao Ren then did not weep.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenjing was eventually ordered to die, Tao Ren did not weep.

sentences.zh: 及太子卒，上履行東宮，見其服玩，大怒，敕有司隨事毀除。

translations.literal: When the crown prince died, the emperor walked through the Eastern Palace, saw his garments and curios, flew into a rage, and ordered the authorities to destroy them item by item.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince's death, the emperor toured the Eastern Palace, saw his lavish belongings, flew into a rage, and ordered officials to destroy them one by one.

sentences.zh: 以竟陵王子良與太子善，而不啟聞，並責之。

translations.literal: Because Prince of Jingling Ziliang was on good terms with the crown prince yet had not reported it, he was rebuked as well.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziliang of Jingling, who had been close to the crown prince yet had not reported his excesses, was rebuked as well.

sentences.zh: 太子素惡西昌侯鸞，嘗謂子良曰：「我意中殊不喜此人，不解其故，當由其福薄故也。」

translations.literal: The crown prince had long disliked Marquis of Xichang Luan; he once told Ziliang: "In my heart I especially dislike this man; I do not understand why—it must be because his fortune is thin."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had long disliked Xiao Luan, Marquis of Xichang; he once told Ziliang, "I have always disliked that man and cannot say why—perhaps his fate is simply too slight.

sentences.zh: 子良為之救解。

translations.literal: Ziliang spoke in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang pleaded on Luan's behalf.

sentences.zh: 及鸞得政，太子子孫無遺焉。

translations.literal: When Luan seized power, none of the crown prince's descendants survived.
translations.idiomatic: When Luan seized power, he left none of the crown prince's descendants alive.

sentences.zh: 二月，魏主始耕藉田於平城南。

translations.literal: In the second month, the Wei emperor for the first time plowed the sacred field south of Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the Wei emperor plowed the sacred field for the first time south of Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史王奐惡寧蠻長史劉興祖，收繫獄，誣其構扇山蠻，欲為亂，敕送興祖下建康；

translations.literal: Governor of Yong Province Wang Huan hated Chief Clerk of Pacifying the Barbarians Liu Xingzu, imprisoned him, and falsely accused him of inciting the mountain barbarians to rebel; he ordered Xingzu sent down to Jiankang;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan, governor of Yong Province, hated Liu Xingzu, chief clerk for pacifying the barbarians; he jailed him on false charges of inciting mountain tribes to revolt and ordered him sent to Jiankang;

sentences.zh: 奐於獄中殺之，詐雲自經。

translations.literal: Huan killed him in prison and falsely claimed he had hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Huan killed him in prison and claimed he had hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，遣中書舍人呂文顯、直閣將軍曹道剛將齋仗五百人收奐，敕鎮西司馬曹虎從江陵步道會襄陽。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and sent Palace Attendant Lü Wenxian and Direct-Palace General Cao Daogang with five hundred armed guards to arrest Huan, ordering Pacifying-the-West Chief of Staff Cao Hu to march overland from Jiangling and join at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and sent Palace Attendant Lü Wenxian and Direct-Palace General Cao Daogang with five hundred armed guards to arrest Wang Huan, while ordering Pacifying-the-West chief of staff Cao Hu to march overland from Jiangling and rendezvous at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 奐子彪，素凶險，奐不能制。

translations.literal: Huan's son Biao was by nature fierce and dangerous; Huan could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's son Wang Biao was violent and reckless by nature, and Huan could not control him.

sentences.zh: 長史殷睿，奐之婿也。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Yin Rui was Huan's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Yin Rui was Huan's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 謂奐曰：「曹、呂來，既不見真敕，恐為奸變，正宜錄取，馳啟聞耳。」

translations.literal: He said to Huan: "When Cao and Lü come, since we have not seen the true edict, we fear a treacherous turn; we ought to seize them and send a swift report."
translations.idiomatic: He told Huan, "Cao and Lü are coming without a verifiable edict—we may be facing a coup. We should seize them and send an urgent report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 奐納之。

translations.literal: Huan accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Huan agreed.

sentences.zh: 彪輒發州兵千餘人，開庫配甲仗，出南堂，陳兵，閉門拒守。

translations.literal: Biao immediately mobilized more than a thousand provincial troops, opened the armory to issue armor and weapons, went out to the Southern Hall, arrayed troops, closed the gates, and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Biao at once mobilized over a thousand provincial troops, opened the armory to issue arms, deployed men in the Southern Hall, shut the gates, and prepared to resist.

sentences.zh: 奐門生鄭羽叩頭啟奐，乞出城迎台使，奐曰：「我不作賊，欲先遣啟自申；

translations.literal: Huan's student Zheng Yu kowtowed and urged Huan to go out and welcome the imperial envoys; Huan said: "I am not making rebellion; I wish first to send a report to explain myself;
translations.idiomatic: Huan's protégé Zheng Yu kowtowed and begged him to go out and welcome the imperial envoys; Huan said, "I am no rebel—I mean first to send a memorial explaining myself;

sentences.zh: 正恐曹、呂輩小人相陵藉，故且閉門自守耳。」

translations.literal: I only fear that petty men like Cao and Lü will bully and insult us, so for now I close the gates and hold myself."
translations.idiomatic: I only fear petty men like Cao and Lü will abuse us, so for now I am merely holding the gates closed.

sentences.zh: 彪遂出，與虎軍戰，兵敗，走歸。

translations.literal: Biao then went out, fought Cao Hu's army, was defeated, and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Biao then sallied out, fought Cao Hu's troops, was beaten, and fled back inside.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙亥，司馬黃瑤起、寧蠻長史河東裴叔業於城內起兵，攻奐，斬之，執彪及弟爽、弼、殷睿，皆伏誅。

translations.literal: In the third month, on yihai, Chief of Staff Huang Yaoqi and Chief Clerk of Pacifying the Barbarians Pei Shuye of Hedong rose in arms within the city, attacked Huan, beheaded him, seized Biao and his brothers Shuang, Bi, and Yin Rui, and all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yihai, chief of staff Huang Yaoqi and pacifying-the-barbarians chief clerk Pei Shuye of Hedong mutinied inside the city, attacked Wang Huan, and killed him; they seized Biao, his brothers Shuang and Bi, and Yin Rui, and all were put to death.

sentences.zh: 彪兄融、琛死於建康，琛弟秘書丞肅獨得脫，奔魏。

translations.literal: Biao's elder brothers Rong and Chen died at Jiankang; Chen's younger brother, Secretariat Director Su, alone escaped and fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Biao's elder brothers Rong and Chen were killed at Jiankang; Chen's younger brother Su, a director in the secretariat, alone escaped and fled to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲午，立南郡王昭業為皇太孫，東宮文武悉改為太孫官屬，以太子妃琅邪王氏為皇太孫太妃，南郡王妃何氏為皇太孫妃。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiawu, Prince of Nanjun Zhaoye was established as imperial great-grandson; all Eastern Palace civil and military offices were changed to great-grandson staff; the crown prince's consort, Lady Wang of Langye, was made great-grandson grand consort; the Prince of Nanjun's consort, Lady He, was made great-grandson consort.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiawu, Prince Zhaoye of Nan Commandery was named imperial great-grandson; Eastern Palace officials were retitled as great-grandson staff; the late crown prince's consort, Lady Wang of Langye, became great-grandson grand consort; and Prince Zhaoye's consort, Lady He, became great-grandson consort.

sentences.zh: 妃戢，之女也。

translations.literal: The consort was the daughter of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Lady He was a daughter of the Ji clan.

sentences.zh: 魏太尉丕等請建中宮，戊戌，立皇后馮氏。

translations.literal: Wei Grand Commandant Pi and others requested establishing the central palace; on wuxu, Empress Feng was established.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei's Grand Commandant Yuan Pi and others petitioned to establish an empress; on wuxu, Lady Feng was made empress.

sentences.zh: 後，熙之女也。

translations.literal: The empress was the daughter of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: She was a daughter of Feng Xi.

sentences.zh: 魏主以《白虎通》云：「王者不臣妻之父母」，下詔令太師上書不稱臣，入朝不拜；

translations.literal: The Wei emperor, citing the Baihu tong: "A king does not treat his wife's parents as subjects," issued an edict that the Grand Preceptor in memorials should not call himself subject and in court should not bow;
translations.idiomatic: Citing the Baihu tong—"A king does not treat his wife's parents as subjects"—the Wei emperor decreed that Grand Preceptor Feng Xi need not style himself a subject in memorials or bow when entering court;

sentences.zh: 熙固辭。

translations.literal: Xi firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xi firmly declined the privilege.

sentences.zh: 光城蠻帥征虜將軍田益宗帥部落四千餘戶叛，降於魏。

translations.literal: Tian Yizong, barbarian chief of Guangcheng and General Who Punishes the Barbarians, led more than four thousand households of his tribe in rebellion and surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yizong, a Guangcheng tribal chief holding the title General Who Punishes the Barbarians, led more than four thousand households in revolt and surrendered to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬戌，魏主宴四廟子孫於宣文堂，親與之齒，用家人禮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on renxu, the Wei emperor feasted the descendants of the four temples in the Xuwen Hall, personally matching their ages and using family ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renxu, the Wei emperor entertained imperial clansmen from all four ancestral temples in the Hall of Promoting Culture, seating himself by their ages and treating them with family courtesy.

sentences.zh: 甲子，魏主臨朝堂，引公卿以下決疑政，錄囚徒。

translations.literal: On jiazi, the Wei emperor attended the court hall, summoned the nobles and officials and below to decide doubtful policies, and reviewed prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, the Wei emperor held court, called dukes and officials to settle doubtful matters of policy, and reviewed prisoners.

sentences.zh: 帝謂司空穆亮曰：「自今朝廷政事，日中以前，卿等先自論議；

translations.literal: The emperor said to Minister of Works Mu Liang: "From now on, on court affairs, before noon you shall first deliberate among yourselves;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Minister of Works Mu Liang, "From now on, on court business before noon you are to deliberate among yourselves first;

sentences.zh: 日中以後，朕與卿等共決之。」

translations.literal: After noon, I together with you shall jointly decide them."
translations.idiomatic: after noon I shall decide them together with you."

sentences.zh: 丙子，以宜都王鏗為南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Prince of Yidu Keng was appointed Governor of Southern Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Prince Keng of Yidu was appointed governor of Southern Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 先是廬陵王子卿為南豫州刺史，之鎮，道中戲部伍為水軍；

translations.literal: Earlier Prince of Luling Ziqing had been Governor of Southern Yu Province; on the way to his post he playfully drilled his retinue as a naval force;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Prince Ziqing of Luling had been governor of Southern Yu Province; on the road to his post he playfully drilled his escort as a naval force;

sentences.zh: 上聞之，大怒，殺其典簽，以鏗代之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he was greatly angered, executed his chief clerk, and replaced him with Keng.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this, he flew into a rage, executed Ziqing's chief clerk, and replaced him with Keng.

sentences.zh: 子卿還第，上終身不與相見。

translations.literal: Ziqing returned to his residence; the emperor never met with him again for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqing returned home; the emperor never saw him again for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 襄陽蠻首雷婆思等帥戶千餘求內徙於魏，魏人處之沔北。

translations.literal: Lei Posi and other Xiangyang barbarian chiefs led more than a thousand households seeking inward migration to Wei; the Wei settled them north of the Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Posi and other Xiangyang tribal chiefs led more than a thousand households seeking resettlement within Wei territory; the Wei placed them north of the Han.

sentences.zh: 魏主以平城地寒，六月雨雪，風沙常起，將遷都洛陽；

translations.literal: The Wei emperor, considering Pingcheng's land cold, with rain and snow in the sixth month and wind and sand constantly rising, intended to move the capital to Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor found Pingcheng too cold—rain and snow even in the sixth month, wind and sand constant—and planned to move the capital to Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 恐群臣不從，乃議大舉伐齊，欲以脅眾。

translations.literal: fearing the nobles and officials would not follow, he then discussed a great campaign against Qi, intending to coerce the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: fearing his ministers would resist, he proposed a major campaign against Qi to bring them into line.

sentences.zh: 齋於明堂左個，使太常卿王諶筮之，遇「革」，帝曰：「『湯、武革命，順乎天而應乎人。』

translations.literal: He fasted in the left bay of the Bright Hall, had Director of Ceremonies Wang Chen divine, and obtained "Revolution"; the emperor said: "'Tang and Wu carried out revolution, accordant with Heaven and responsive to men.
translations.idiomatic: He fasted in the left bay of the Bright Hall and had Director of Ceremonies Wang Chen cast the oracle, which yielded the hexagram Revolution; the emperor said, "'Tang and Wu carried out revolution, accordant with Heaven and responsive to the people.

sentences.zh: 吉孰大焉！」

translations.literal: What auspice could be greater!"
translations.idiomatic: What omen could be more auspicious!'

sentences.zh: 群臣莫敢言。

translations.literal: None of the nobles and officials dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: None of the assembled ministers dared object.

sentences.zh: 尚書任城王澄曰：「陛下弈葉重光，帝有中土；

translations.literal: Minister of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, said: "Your Majesty's line has renewed its radiance generation after generation and rules the central land;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Masters of Writing Yuan Cheng, Prince of Rencheng, said, "Your Majesty's house has renewed its radiance generation after generation and already rules the central lands;

sentences.zh: 今出師以征未服，而得湯、武革命之象，未為全吉也。」

translations.literal: now to march out and campaign against those not yet submitted, yet obtain the image of Tang and Wu's revolution—is not wholly auspicious."
translations.idiomatic: to march out now against unsubdued foes yet draw the image of Tang and Wu's revolution is not wholly auspicious.

sentences.zh: 帝厲聲曰：「繇云：『大人虎變』，何言不吉！」

translations.literal: The emperor said sharply: "The commentary says: 'The great man transforms like a tiger'—how can you say it is not auspicious!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped, "The commentary says, 'The great man transforms like a tiger'—how can you call that inauspicious!

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「陛下龍興已久，何得今乃虎變！」

translations.literal: Cheng said: "Your Majesty's dragon rise was long ago—how can you now be tiger-transforming!"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, "Your Majesty's dragon rise was long ago—how can you be transforming like a tiger only now!

sentences.zh: 帝作色曰：「社稷我之社稷，任城欲沮眾邪！」

translations.literal: The emperor changed color and said: "The altars of soil and grain are my altars of soil and grain—does Rencheng wish to discourage the multitude!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flushed and said, "The realm is mine—does Prince of Rencheng mean to discourage the army!

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「社稷雖為陛下之有，臣為社稷之臣，安可知危而不言！」

translations.literal: Cheng said: "Although the altars of soil and grain belong to Your Majesty, I am a subject of the altars of soil and grain—how can I know danger and not speak!"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "Though the realm belongs to Your Majesty, I am its subject—how can I see peril and stay silent!

sentences.zh: 帝久之乃解，曰：「各言其志，夫亦何傷！」

translations.literal: After a long while the emperor relented and said: "Each speak his mind—what harm is there!"
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the emperor relented. "Speak your minds," he said—"what harm is there in that?"

sentences.zh: 既還宮，召澄入見，逆謂之曰：「向者《革卦》，今當更與卿論之。

translations.literal: When he had returned to the palace, he summoned Cheng to an audience and, going to meet him, said: "As to the Revolution hexagram just now, I ought to discuss it further with you.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the palace he summoned Cheng and, going out to meet him, said, "About the Revolution hexagram just now—I should discuss it further with you.

sentences.zh: 明堂之忿，恐人人競言，沮我大計，故以聲色怖文武耳。

translations.literal: My anger in the Bright Hall—I feared everyone would compete in speech and discourage my great plan, so I used voice and countenance to frighten the civil and military officials, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: My anger in the Bright Hall was feigned—I feared everyone would speak up and block my great plan, so I used harsh words to frighten the court, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 想識朕意。」

translations.literal: I trust you understand my intent."
translations.idiomatic: I trust you understand my intent.

sentences.zh: 因屏人，謂澄曰：「今日之舉，誠為不易。

translations.literal: He then dismissed attendants and said to Cheng: "Today's undertaking is truly not easy.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed everyone else and told Cheng, "What I mean to do today is truly no small matter.

sentences.zh: 但國家興自朔土，徙居平城；

translations.literal: But the state rose from the northern lands and moved to dwell at Pingcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Our state arose in the northern frontier and moved its seat to Pingcheng;

sentences.zh: 此乃用武之地，非可文治。

translations.literal: this is a land for wielding arms, not for civil governance.
translations.idiomatic: that is a land for wielding arms, not for civil rule.

sentences.zh: 今將移風易俗，其道誠難，朕欲因此遷宅中原，卿以為何如？」

translations.literal: Now we are to change customs and transform habits—the path is truly difficult. I wish to take this opportunity to move our seat to the Central Plains. What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Changing customs and habits is truly hard. I mean to seize this moment and move our capital to the Central Plains—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「陛下欲卜宅中土，以經略四海，此周、漢之所以興隆也。」

translations.literal: Cheng said: "Your Majesty wishes to choose a seat in the Central Land and strategize over the four seas—this is how Zhou and Han rose to greatness."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng replied, "Your Majesty means to establish the capital in the heartland and extend rule over the four seas—that is how Zhou and Han achieved their greatness.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「北人習常戀故，必將驚擾，奈何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Northerners are accustomed to the old ways and attached to their homes—they will surely be alarmed and disturbed. What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Northerners cling to custom and old homes—they will panic and resist. What can be done?

sentences.zh: 澄曰：「非常之事，故非常人之所及。

translations.literal: Cheng said: "An extraordinary undertaking is therefore beyond ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "An extraordinary task lies beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 陛下斷自聖心，彼亦何所能為！」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty decides from your sage heart, what can they possibly do!"
translations.idiomatic: Once Your Majesty decides from your own sage judgment, what can they do?

sentences.zh: 帝曰；

translations.literal: The emperor said;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said;

sentences.zh: 「任城，吾之子房也！」

translations.literal: "Rencheng—you are my Zifang!"
translations.idiomatic: Rencheng, you are my Zhang Liang!"

sentences.zh: 六月，丙戌，命作河橋，欲以濟師。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingxu, he ordered a river bridge built to ferry troops across.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day bingxu, he ordered a bridge built over the river to move his army across.

sentences.zh: 秘書監盧淵上表，以為：「前世承平之主，未嘗親御六軍，決勝行陳之間；

translations.literal: Secretary Supervisor Lu Yuan submitted a memorial stating: "Emperors of past ages in times of peace never personally commanded the Six Armies or decided victory amid the battle lines;
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Supervisor Lu Yuan submitted a memorial arguing that emperors of earlier peaceful ages never personally led the Six Armies or decided battles in the field;

sentences.zh: 豈非勝之不足為武，不勝有虧威望乎！

translations.literal: is it not that victory would add little to martial renown, while defeat would damage imperial prestige?
translations.idiomatic: for victory would scarcely enhance martial glory, while defeat would tarnish imperial prestige.

sentences.zh: 昔魏武以弊卒一萬破袁紹，謝玄以步兵三千摧苻秦，勝負之變，決於須臾，不在眾寡也。」

translations.literal: In former days Cao Cao broke Yuan Shao with ten thousand worn troops; Xie Xuan shattered Fu Qin's forces with three thousand foot soldiers—the turn of victory and defeat is decided in an instant, not by numbers."
translations.idiomatic: In the past Cao Cao defeated Yuan Shao with ten thousand exhausted troops, and Xie Xuan crushed Fu Qin's army with three thousand infantry—the outcome turns in a moment, not on numbers alone.

sentences.zh: 詔報曰：「承平之主，所以不親戎事者，或以同軌無敵，或以懦劣偷安。

translations.literal: The edict replied: "Emperors in peaceful times did not personally take to arms either because all lands submitted and there were no enemies, or because they were weak and sought idle comfort.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial reply said, "Peaceful emperors stayed away from war either because the realm was united and they had no foe, or because they were timid and sought ease.

sentences.zh: 今謂之同軌則未然，比之懦劣則可恥，必若王者不當親戎，則先王制革輅，何所施也？

translations.literal: To call our case the former is not yet so; to compare us to the latter is shameful. If a true king ought not to take the field personally, then to what purpose did the former kings ordain the leather war chariot?
translations.idiomatic: Neither description fits us today—the first is not yet true, and the second would be shameful. If a true king should never take the field, why did the ancient kings establish the leather war chariot?

sentences.zh: 魏武之勝，蓋由仗順，苻氏之敗，亦由失政；

translations.literal: Cao Cao's victory was largely because he had righteousness on his side; the Fu clan's defeat was also due to misgovernment;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao won because he had justice on his side, and the Fu clan fell because it lost the way of governance;

sentences.zh: 豈寡必能勝眾，弱必能制強邪！」

translations.literal: how could the few necessarily overcome the many, or the weak necessarily control the strong!"
translations.idiomatic: surely the few do not always defeat the many, nor the weak always master the strong!

sentences.zh: 丁未，魏主講武，命尚書李沖典武選。

translations.literal: On dingwei the Wei sovereign held a military review and ordered Minister of Works Li Chong to oversee selection for martial service.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingwei the Wei emperor held a military review and put Minister of Works Li Chong in charge of selecting troops.

sentences.zh: 建康僧法智與徐州民周盤龍等作亂，夜，攻徐州城，入之；

translations.literal: The monk Fazhi of Jiankang and Zhou Panlong of Xuzhou and others rebelled; by night they attacked Xuzhou city and entered it;
translations.idiomatic: The monk Fazhi of Jiankang and Zhou Panlong, a commoner of Xuzhou, and others rose in rebellion; by night they attacked Xuzhou city and took it;

sentences.zh: 刺史王玄邈討誅之。

translations.literal: Governor Wang Xuanyao suppressed and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Xuanyao put down the revolt and executed the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸丑，魏立皇子恂為太子。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on guichou, Wei installed the prince Xun as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day guichou, Wei enthroned Prince Xun as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 戊午，魏中外戒嚴，發露布及移書，稱當南伐。

translations.literal: On wuwu Wei declared martial law throughout court and realm, issued open proclamations and diplomatic letters announcing a southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuwu Wei put the court and realm on alert, issued public proclamations and diplomatic letters, and announced a coming southern invasion.

sentences.zh: 詔發揚、徐州民丁，廣設召募以備之。

translations.literal: An edict mobilized labor from Yang and Xu provinces and widely opened recruitment to prepare against it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict mobilized laborers from Yang and Xu provinces and opened wide recruitment to prepare defenses.

sentences.zh: 中書郎王融，自恃人地，三十內望為公輔。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat Wang Rong, relying on his birth and standing, expected to reach the highest ministerial posts before thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong, an attendant gentleman of the Secretariat, counted on his family and status and expected to reach the highest offices before he turned thirty.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜直省中，撫案歎曰：「為爾寂寂，鄧禹笑人！」

translations.literal: Once while on night duty in the secretariat, he leaned on his desk and sighed: "To end up so obscure—Deng Yu would laugh at me!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, on night duty in the secretariat, he leaned on his desk and sighed, "To live so obscurely—Deng Yu would laugh at me!

sentences.zh: 行逢朱雀桁開，喧湫不得進，捶車壁歎曰：「車前無八騶，何得稱丈夫！」

translations.literal: As he went out he met the Vermilion Bird Bridge raised and the crowd so dense he could not pass; he beat the carriage wall and sighed: "No eight outriders before my carriage—how can I call myself a true man!"
translations.idiomatic: On his way out he found the Vermilion Bird Bridge raised and the throng so thick he could not pass; he pounded the carriage wall and sighed, "No eight outriders before my carriage—how can I call myself a man!

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良愛其文學，特親厚之。

translations.literal: Prince Ziliang of Jingling admired his literary talent and treated him with special intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziliang of Jingling admired his literary gifts and treated him with exceptional warmth.

sentences.zh: 融見上有北伐之志，數上書獎勸，因大習騎射。

translations.literal: Rong saw that the emperor had a mind to campaign north and repeatedly submitted memorials urging it on; he therefore trained intensively in horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the emperor wished to campaign north, Rong repeatedly submitted memorials urging him on and trained hard in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 及魏將入寇，子良於東府募兵，版融寧朔將軍，使典其事。

translations.literal: When Wei was about to invade, Ziliang recruited troops at the Eastern Headquarters and appointed Rong General Who Calms the North, putting him in charge of the effort.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei was about to invade, Ziliang raised troops at the Eastern Headquarters, commissioned Rong as General Who Calms the North, and put him in charge of recruitment.

sentences.zh: 融傾意招納，得江西傖楚數百人，並有干用。

translations.literal: Rong recruited wholeheartedly and gathered several hundred Jiangxi migrants, all capable and useful.
translations.idiomatic: Rong recruited with all his energy and gathered several hundred hardy men from Jiangxi, all of them capable and useful.

sentences.zh: 會上不豫，詔子良甲仗入延昌殿侍醫藥；

translations.literal: Just then the emperor fell ill; an edict allowed Ziliang to enter the Hall of Extended Splendor armed to attend and administer medicine;
translations.idiomatic: Just then the emperor fell ill, and an edict permitted Ziliang to enter the Hall of Extended Splendor in armor to attend him and oversee his medicine;

sentences.zh: 子良以蕭衍、范雲等皆為帳內軍主。

translations.literal: Ziliang appointed Xiao Yan, Fan Yun, and others as military commanders within his tent guard.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang made Xiao Yan, Fan Yun, and others commanders of the guard within his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，遣江州刺史陳顯達鎮樊城。

translations.literal: On wuchen he sent Jiang Province Governor Chen Xianda to garrison Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuchen he sent Jiang Province Governor Chen Xianda to hold Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 上慮朝野憂遑，力疾召木府奏正聲伎。

translations.literal: The emperor, fearing anxiety in court and country, forced himself despite illness to summon the Music Office to perform orthodox pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing panic in court and country, the emperor forced himself despite illness to summon the Music Office to perform orthodox music.

sentences.zh: 子良日夜在內，太孫間日參承。

translations.literal: Ziliang stayed within day and night; the crown prince visited at intervals to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang remained inside day and night, while the crown prince came every other day to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，上疾亟，暫絕；

translations.literal: On wuyin the emperor's illness turned critical and he briefly lost consciousness;
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuyin the emperor's illness turned grave and he briefly lost consciousness;

sentences.zh: 太孫未入，內外惶懼，百僚皆已變服。

translations.literal: The crown prince had not yet entered; inside and outside were filled with fear, and all officials had already changed into mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had not yet arrived; court and palace were seized with fear, and all the officials had already changed into mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 王融欲矯詔立子良，詔草已立。

translations.literal: Wang Rong wished to forge an edict making Ziliang emperor; the draft was already prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong wanted to forge an edict enthroning Ziliang, and the draft was already written.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍謂范雲曰：「道路籍籍，皆雲將有非常之舉。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan said to Fan Yun: "The roads are buzzing—all say something extraordinary is about to happen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan said to Fan Yun, "The streets are full of rumor—everyone says something extraordinary is coming.

sentences.zh: 王元長非濟世才，視其敗也。」

translations.literal: Wang Yuanzhang is no talent to save the age—we shall see his ruin."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanzhang is no statesman—watch him fail.

sentences.zh: 雲曰：「憂國家者，唯有王中書耳。」

translations.literal: Yun said: "The one who cares for the state is none but Secretary Wang."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun said, "The only one who cares for the state is Secretary Wang.

sentences.zh: 衍曰：「憂國，欲為周、召，欲為豎刁邪？」

translations.literal: Yan said: "Caring for the state—does he mean to be like the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, or like Duke Huan's eunuch?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan said, "Caring for the state—is he trying to be the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, or Duke Huan's eunuch?

sentences.zh: 雲不敢答。

translations.literal: Yun did not dare reply.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yun did not dare answer.

sentences.zh: 及太孫來，王融戎服絳衫，於中書省閣口斷東宮仗不得進。

translations.literal: When the crown prince arrived, Wang Rong in martial dress and a scarlet shirt blocked the Eastern Palace guard at the gate of the Secretariat, barring them from entering.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince arrived, Wang Rong, dressed for battle in a scarlet shirt, blocked the Eastern Palace guard at the Secretariat gate and would not let them pass.

sentences.zh: 頃之，上復甦，問太孫所在，因召東宮器甲皆入，以朝事委尚書左僕射西昌侯鸞。

translations.literal: Shortly after, the emperor revived and asked where the crown prince was; he then summoned the Eastern Palace guards with their weapons inside and entrusted court affairs to Left Vice Minister of Works, Marquis of Xichang, Luan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor revived and asked where the crown prince was; he then summoned the Eastern Palace guard, weapons and all, and entrusted court affairs to Left Vice Minister of Works, Marquis of Xichang, Luan.

sentences.zh: 俄而上殂，融處分以子良兵禁諸門。

translations.literal: Soon the emperor died; Rong deployed Ziliang's troops to seal every gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor died, and Rong used Ziliang's troops to seal every gate.

sentences.zh: 鸞聞之，急馳至雲龍門，不得進，鸞曰：「有敕召我！」

translations.literal: Luan heard and galloped to the Cloud Dragon Gate but could not enter; Luan said: "There is an imperial order summoning me!"
translations.idiomatic: When Luan heard this he galloped to the Cloud Dragon Gate but could not get through; he cried, "I have been summoned by imperial order!

sentences.zh: 排之而入，奉太孫登殿，命左右扶出子良；

translations.literal: He pushed through and entered, escorted the crown prince to the throne, and ordered attendants to lead Ziliang out;
translations.idiomatic: He forced his way in, escorted the crown prince to the throne, and ordered attendants to lead Ziliang away;

sentences.zh: 指麾部署，音響如鐘，殿中無不從命。

translations.literal: His commands rang out like a bell; everyone in the hall obeyed without exception.
translations.idiomatic: His orders rang out like a bell, and everyone in the hall obeyed.

sentences.zh: 融知不遂，釋服還省，歎曰：「公誤我！」

translations.literal: Rong knew his plan had failed; he changed back from mourning dress and returned to the Secretariat, sighing: "My lord—you have ruined me!"
translations.idiomatic: Rong saw that his plan had failed, changed out of mourning dress, returned to the Secretariat, and sighed, "My lord, you have led me astray!

sentences.zh: 由是鬱林王深怨之。

translations.literal: From this Emperor Yulin deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: From that time on Emperor Yulin deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 遺詔曰：「太孫進德日茂，社稷有寄。

translations.literal: The testamentary edict said: "The crown prince's virtue grows daily; the altars of state have one to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: The testamentary edict said, "The crown prince's virtue grows daily, and the altars of state have one to rely on.

sentences.zh: 子良善相毘輔，思弘治道，內外眾事，無大小悉與鸞參懷，共下意！

translations.literal: Ziliang excels at assisting and supporting—let him strive to expand good governance; all affairs within and without, great and small alike, consult with Luan and share your intentions!
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang is well suited to assist and support—let him strive to broaden good governance; on all matters within and without, great and small alike, consult with Luan and share your intentions!

sentences.zh: 尚書中事，職務根本，悉委右僕射王晏、吏部尚書徐孝嗣；

translations.literal: Affairs within the Secretariat, the root of office, entrust entirely to Right Vice Minister Wang Yan and Minister of Civil Appointments Xu Xiaosi;
translations.idiomatic: Affairs of the Secretariat, the root of government, entrust wholly to Right Vice Minister Wang Yan and Minister of Civil Appointments Xu Xiaosi;

sentences.zh: 軍旅之略，委王敬則、陳顯達、王廣之、王玄邈、沈文季、張瑰、薛淵等。」

translations.literal: Military strategy entrust to Wang Jingze, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, Wang Xuanyao, Shen Wenji, Zhang Gui, Xue Yuan, and the rest."
translations.idiomatic: Military affairs entrust to Wang Jingze, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, Wang Xuanyao, Shen Wenji, Zhang Gui, Xue Yuan, and the rest."

sentences.zh: 世祖留心政事，務總大體，嚴明有斷，郡縣久於其職，長吏犯法，封刃行誅。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu attended closely to governance, keeping to the broad essentials, strict and clear in judgment; prefectures and counties held their posts for long terms, and when chief officials broke the law he ordered immediate execution.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu attended closely to governance, keeping to the broad essentials with strict and decisive judgment; prefectures and counties kept their officials in office for long terms, and when local leaders broke the law he had them executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 故永明之世，百姓豐樂，賊盜屏息。

translations.literal: Therefore in the Yongming era the people were prosperous and content, and bandits and thieves vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in the Yongming era the people were prosperous and content, and bandits and thieves disappeared.

sentences.zh: 然頗好游宴，華靡之事，常言恨之，未能頓遣。

translations.literal: Yet he was rather fond of feasting and touring, and of luxuriant extravagance; he often spoke of regretting it but could not abandon it all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was rather fond of feasting and touring and of lavish display; he often said he regretted it but could not give it up all at once.

sentences.zh: 鬱林王之未立也，眾皆疑立子良，口語喧騰。

translations.literal: Before Emperor Yulin was enthroned, everyone suspected Ziliang would be made emperor, and rumors ran wild.
translations.idiomatic: Before Emperor Yulin was enthroned, everyone suspected that Ziliang would be made emperor, and rumors swirled.

sentences.zh: 武陵王曄於眾中大言曰：「若立民，則應在我；

translations.literal: Prince of Wuling Ye declared loudly before the assembly: "If a commoner is to be enthroned, it ought to be me;
translations.idiomatic: Before the assembly Prince Ye of Wuling declared loudly, "If a lesser prince is to be enthroned, it should be me;

sentences.zh: 立嫡，則應在太孫。」

translations.literal: if the legitimate heir is enthroned, it ought to be the crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: if the rightful heir is enthroned, it should be the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 由是帝深憑賴之。

translations.literal: From this the emperor relied on him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: From this the emperor came to rely on him deeply.

sentences.zh: 直閣周奉叔、曹道剛素為帝心膂，並使監殿中直衛；

translations.literal: Chamberlain Attendant Zhou Fengshu and Cao Daogang had long been the emperor's trusted right hands; both were made to oversee the direct palace guard;
translations.idiomatic: Chamber Attendants Zhou Fengshu and Cao Daogang had long been the emperor's trusted confidants; both were put in charge of the palace guard;

sentences.zh: 少日，復以道剛為黃門郎。

translations.literal: A few days later Daogang was again appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Daogang was again made Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 初，西昌侯鸞為太祖所愛，鸞性儉素，車服儀從，同於素士，所居官名為嚴能，故世祖亦重之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Marquis of Xichang Luan had been beloved by Emperor Gao; Luan was frugal and plain—carriages, robes, and retinue matched those of common scholars—and wherever he served his reputation was for strict capability; therefore Emperor Wu also valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Marquis Luan of Xichang had been favored by Emperor Gao; Luan was frugal and plain, his carriage, dress, and retinue no different from an ordinary scholar's, and in every office he held he was known for strict competence—so Emperor Wu also valued him.

sentences.zh: 世祖遺詔，使竟陵王子良輔政，鸞知尚書事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu's testamentary edict had Prince Ziliang of Jingling assist in governance and Luan oversee Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's testamentary edict had Prince Ziliang of Jingling assist in governance and Luan oversee Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 子良素仁厚，不樂世務，乃更推鸞，故遺詔云「事無大小，悉與鸞參懷」，子良之志也。

translations.literal: Ziliang was naturally kind and generous and took no joy in worldly affairs; he therefore pushed authority further toward Luan—hence the testamentary lines "all affairs great and small alike consult with Luan" reflected Ziliang's own wish.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang was naturally kind and generous and took no pleasure in worldly affairs, so he pushed authority toward Luan; hence the testament's words, "on all matters great and small alike consult with Luan," reflected Ziliang's own wish.

sentences.zh: 帝少養於子良妃袁氏，慈愛甚著。

translations.literal: The emperor had been raised from childhood by Ziliang's consort, Lady Yuan, and their affection was well known.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had been raised from childhood by Ziliang's consort, Lady Yuan, and their mutual affection was well known.

sentences.zh: 及王融有謀，遂深忌子良。

translations.literal: After Wang Rong's plot, he came to deeply mistrust Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Rong's plot, he came to deeply mistrust Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 大行出太極殿，子良居中書省，帝使虎賁中郎將潘敞領二百人仗屯太極西階以防之。

translations.literal: When the imperial coffin was borne out of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, Ziliang remained in the Secretariat; the emperor sent Captain of the Tiger Guard Pan Chang with two hundred armed men to station on the western steps of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial coffin was borne out of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, Ziliang remained in the Secretariat; the emperor sent Captain of the Tiger Guard Pan Chang with two hundred armed men to hold the western steps of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and guard against him.

sentences.zh: 既成服，諸王皆出，子良乞停至山陵，不許。

translations.literal: After mourning dress was completed, all princes were to leave the capital; Ziliang asked to stay until the imperial tomb was completed but was refused.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period was complete, all the princes were to leave the capital; Ziliang asked to remain until the imperial tomb was finished, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 壬午，稱遺詔，以武陵王曄為衛將軍，與征南大將軍陳顯達並開府儀同三司；

translations.literal: On renwu, by testamentary edict Prince of Wuling Ye was made Defender-General, and together with General Who Conquers the South Chen Xianda received the honors of an independent command equal to the Three Excellencies;
translations.idiomatic: On the day renwu, by testamentary edict Prince Ye of Wuling was made Defender-General and, together with General Who Conquers the South Chen Xianda, granted an independent command equal to the Three Excellencies;

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射、西昌侯鸞為尚書令；

translations.literal: Left Vice Minister of Works, Marquis of Xichang Luan, became Director of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Minister of Works, Marquis Luan of Xichang, was made Director of the Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 太孫詹事沈文季為護軍。

translations.literal: Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince Shen Wenji became Guardian-General.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince Shen Wenji was made Guardian-General.

sentences.zh: 癸未，以竟陵王子良為太傅；

translations.literal: On guiwei Prince Ziliang of Jingling was made Grand Tutor;
translations.idiomatic: On the day guiwei Prince Ziliang of Jingling was made Grand Tutor;

sentences.zh: 蠲除三調及眾逋，省御府及無用池田、邸治。

translations.literal: Taxes of three categories and all arrears were remitted; imperial storehouses and unused ponds, fields, and lodges were reduced;
translations.idiomatic: Taxes of three categories and all arrears were remitted; imperial storehouses and unused ponds, fields, and lodges were cut back;

sentences.zh: 減關市徵稅。

translations.literal: Levies at passes and markets were lowered.
translations.idiomatic: Levies at passes and markets were reduced.

sentences.zh: 先是，蠲原之詔，多無事實，督責如故。

translations.literal: Before this, edicts remitting taxes and land often had no real effect; collection and enforcement continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, edicts remitting taxes and land often amounted to nothing; collection and enforcement continued as before.

sentences.zh: 是時西昌侯鸞知政，恩信兩行，眾皆悅之。

translations.literal: Now Marquis of Xichang Luan held the reins of government; favor and trust both flowed, and everyone was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Now Marquis Luan of Xichang held the reins of government; favor and trust went hand in hand, and everyone was pleased.

sentences.zh: 魏山陽景桓公尉元卒。

translations.literal: In Wei, Marquis Jingzhuang of Shanyang, Wei Yuan, died.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei, Wei Yuan, Marquis Jingzhuang of Shanyang, died.

sentences.zh: 魏主使錄尚書事廣陵王羽持節安撫六鎮，發其突騎。

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign sent Grand Secretary Guangling Wang Yu with credentials to pacify and reassure the Six Garrisons and levy their elite cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor sent Grand Secretary Prince Yu of Guangling with credentials to reassure the Six Garrisons and levy their elite cavalry.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，魏主辭永固陵；

translations.literal: On dinghai the Wei sovereign took leave of Yonggu Mausoleum;
translations.idiomatic: On the day dinghai the Wei emperor took leave of Yonggu Mausoleum;

sentences.zh: 己丑，發平城，南伐，步騎三十餘萬；

translations.literal: On jichou he departed Pingcheng on a southern campaign with more than three hundred thousand infantry and cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: On the day jichou he set out from Pingcheng on a southern campaign with more than three hundred thousand infantry and cavalry;

sentences.zh: 使太尉丕與廣陵王羽留守平城，並加使持節。

translations.literal: He left Grand Commandant Pi and Guangling Wang Yu to hold Pingcheng, both with extraordinary credentials.
translations.idiomatic: He left Grand Commandant Pi and Prince Yu of Guangling to hold Pingcheng, both granted extraordinary credentials.

sentences.zh: 羽曰：「太尉宜專節度，臣正可為副。」

translations.literal: Yu said: "The Grand Commandant ought to hold sole command; I can serve only as his deputy."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "The Grand Commandant should hold sole command; I can serve only as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 魏主曰：「老者之智，少者之決，汝無辭也。」

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign said: "The old have wisdom, the young have resolve—you need make no excuses."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor said, "The old have wisdom, the young have resolve—you need make no excuses.

sentences.zh: 以河南王干為車騎大將軍、都督關右諸軍事，又以司空穆亮、安南將軍盧淵、平南將軍薛胤皆為干副，眾合七萬出子午谷。

translations.literal: He appointed Prince Gan of Henan General of Chariots and Cavalry and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs west of the Pass, and further made Minister of Works Mu Liang, General Who Pacifies the South Lu Yuan, and General Who Pacifies the South Ping Xue Yin all deputies to Gan; their combined force of seventy thousand marched out through Ziwu Valley.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Prince Gan of Henan General of Chariots and Cavalry and commander of all forces west of the Pass, with Minister of Works Mu Liang, General Who Pacifies the South Lu Yuan, and General Who Pacifies the South Xue Yin all serving as Gan's deputies; their combined force of seventy thousand marched out through Ziwu Valley.

sentences.zh: 胤，辯之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yin was the great-grandson of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was the great-grandson of Bian.

sentences.zh: 鬱林王性辯慧，美容止，善應對，哀樂過人；

translations.literal: Prince Yulin was quick-witted and eloquent by nature, handsome in bearing, skilled in repartee, and more expressive in joy and sorrow than others;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yulin was quick-witted and eloquent by nature, handsome in bearing, skilled in repartee, and more expressive in joy and sorrow than others;

sentences.zh: 世祖由是愛之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu therefore loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu therefore favored him.

sentences.zh: 而矯情飾詐，陰懷鄙慝，與左右群小共衣食，同臥起。

translations.literal: Yet he affectingly feigned emotion and practiced deception, secretly harboring base malice; he shared food and clothing with his favored low companions and slept and rose with them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he put on false feeling and practiced deceit, secretly nursing base resentments; he shared food and clothing with the low companions around him and slept and rose together with them.

sentences.zh: 始為南郡王，從竟陵王子良在西州，文惠太子每禁其起居，節其用度。

translations.literal: When he was first Prince of Nanjun, he followed Prince Ziliang of Jingling at Xizhou; Crown Prince Wenhui often restricted his daily conduct and curtailed his expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first Prince of Nanjun, he followed Prince Ziliang of Jingling at Xizhou; Crown Prince Wenhui often restricted his daily conduct and curtailed his expenditures.

sentences.zh: 王密就富人求錢，無敢不與。

translations.literal: The prince secretly approached wealthy men to borrow money, and none dared refuse him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince secretly approached wealthy men to borrow money, and none dared refuse him.

sentences.zh: 別作鑰鉤，夜開西州後閣，與左右至諸營署中淫宴。

translations.literal: He had a separate key-hook made and at night opened the rear gate of Xizhou, going with his companions to various camp offices for licentious feasting.
translations.idiomatic: He had a separate key-hook made and at night opened the rear gate of Xizhou, going with his companions to various camp offices for licentious feasting.

sentences.zh: 師史仁祖、侍書胡天翼相謂曰：「若言之二宮，則其事未易；

translations.literal: Masters Shi Renzu and Hu Tianyi, attendants in the secretariat, said to each other: "If we report this to the two palaces, the matter will not be easily settled;
translations.idiomatic: Masters Shi Renzu and Hu Tianyi, attendants in the secretariat, said to each other, "If we report this to the two palaces, the matter will not be easily settled;

sentences.zh: 若於營署為異人所毆及犬物所傷，豈直罪止一身，亦當盡室及禍。

translations.literal: if in the camp offices we are beaten by strangers or injured by dogs or such things, would the guilt stop with us alone? Our whole households would also suffer disaster.
translations.idiomatic: if in the camp offices we are beaten by strangers or injured by dogs or the like, would the guilt stop with us alone? Our whole households would also be ruined.

sentences.zh: 年各七十，餘生豈足吝邪！」

translations.literal: Each of us is seventy years old—why begrudge what remains of our lives!"
translations.idiomatic: Each of us is seventy years old—why begrudge what little life remains!

sentences.zh: 數日間，二人相繼自殺，二宮不知也。

translations.literal: Within a few days the two men killed themselves in succession, and the two palaces knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days the two men killed themselves in succession, and the two palaces knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 所愛左右，皆逆加官爵，疏於黃紙，使囊盛帶之，許南面之日，依此施行。

translations.literal: Those he favored among his attendants he all in advance conferred rank and titles upon, writing the appointments on yellow paper and having them stored in pouches and carried on their persons, with a promise that when he faced south as emperor these would be put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Those he favored among his attendants he all in advance conferred rank and titles upon, writing the appointments on yellow paper and having them stored in pouches and carried on their persons, with a promise that when he faced south as emperor these would be put into effect.

sentences.zh: 侍太子疾及居喪，憂容號毀，見者嗚咽；

translations.literal: When attending the crown prince in illness and during mourning, his face wore grief and he wailed and emaciated himself; those who saw him sobbed;
translations.idiomatic: When attending the crown prince in illness and during mourning, his face wore grief and he wailed and emaciated himself; those who saw him sobbed;

sentences.zh: 裁還私室，即歡笑酣飲。

translations.literal: but as soon as he returned to his private quarters he laughed merrily and drank deeply.
translations.idiomatic: but as soon as he returned to his private quarters he laughed merrily and drank deeply.

sentences.zh: 常令女巫楊氏禱祀，速求天位。

translations.literal: He constantly had the shamaness Lady Yang perform prayers and sacrifices, urgently seeking the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly had the shamaness Lady Yang perform prayers and sacrifices, urgently seeking the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 及太子卒，謂由楊氏之力，倍加敬倍。

translations.literal: When the crown prince died, he believed it was through Lady Yang's power and redoubled his reverence for her.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince died, he believed it was through Lady Yang's power and redoubled his reverence for her.

sentences.zh: 既為太孫，世祖有疾，又令楊氏禱祀。

translations.literal: Once he became grand heir apparent, when Emperor Shizu fell ill he again had Lady Yang perform prayers and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became grand heir apparent, when Emperor Shizu fell ill he again had Lady Yang perform prayers and sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時何妃猶在西州，世祖疾稍危，太孫與何妃書，紙中央作一大喜字，而作三十六小喜字繞之。

translations.literal: At that time Consort He was still at Xizhou. When Emperor Shizu's illness grew critical, the grand heir wrote to Consort He; in the center of the paper he drew one large character xi for joy, surrounded by thirty-six smaller xi characters.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Consort He was still at Xizhou. When Emperor Shizu's illness grew critical, the grand heir wrote to Consort He; in the center of the paper he drew one large character for joy, surrounded by thirty-six smaller joy characters.

sentences.zh: 侍世祖疾，言發淚下。

translations.literal: When attending Emperor Shizu in his illness, he spoke and tears fell.
translations.idiomatic: When attending Emperor Shizu in his illness, he spoke and tears fell.

sentences.zh: 世祖以為必能負荷大業，謂曰：「五年中一委宰相，汝勿措意；

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu thought he would surely be able to bear the great enterprise and said to him: "For five years leave everything entirely to the chief minister; do not concern yourself;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu thought he would surely be able to bear the great enterprise and said to him, "For five years leave everything entirely to the chief minister; do not concern yourself;

sentences.zh: 五年外勿復委人。

translations.literal: After five years do not entrust matters to others again.
translations.idiomatic: After five years do not entrust matters to others again.

sentences.zh: 若自作無成，無所多恨。」

translations.literal: If you act on your own and achieve nothing, you will have little cause for regret."
translations.idiomatic: If you act on your own and achieve nothing, you will have little cause for regret.

sentences.zh: 臨終，執其手曰：「若憶翁，當好作！」

translations.literal: At the end of his life he took his hand and said: "If you remember your old grandfather, you must do well!"
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his life he took his hand and said, "If you remember your old grandfather, you must do well!

sentences.zh: 遂殂。

translations.literal: Then he died.
translations.idiomatic: Then he died.

sentences.zh: 大斂始畢，悉呼世祖諸伎，備奏眾樂。

translations.literal: As soon as the grand dressing of the corpse was finished, he summoned all of Emperor Shizu's performers and had every sort of music played.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the grand dressing of the corpse was finished, he summoned all of Emperor Shizu's performers and had every sort of music played.

sentences.zh: 即位十餘日，即收王融下廷尉，使中丞孔稚珪奏融險躁輕狡，招納不逞，誹謗朝政。

translations.literal: Within little more than ten days of taking the throne he had Wang Rong arrested and sent to the Minister of Justice; he had Censor-in-Chief Kong Zhigui memorialize that Rong was reckless, volatile, and cunning, that he gathered malcontents, and that he slandered the court and government.
translations.idiomatic: Within little more than ten days of taking the throne he had Wang Rong arrested and sent to the Minister of Justice; he had Censor-in-Chief Kong Zhigui memorialize that Rong was reckless, volatile, and cunning, that he gathered malcontents, and that he slandered the court and government.

sentences.zh: 融求援於竟陵王子良，子良憂懼，不敢救。

translations.literal: Rong sought help from Prince Ziliang of Jingling; Ziliang was anxious and afraid and did not dare save him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong sought help from Prince Ziliang of Jingling; Ziliang was anxious and afraid and did not dare save him.

sentences.zh: 遂於獄賜死，時年二十七。

translations.literal: He was therefore granted death in prison; he was twenty-seven years old at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore granted death in prison; he was twenty-seven years old at the time.

sentences.zh: 初，融欲與東海徐勉相識，每托人召之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Rong had wished to become acquainted with Xu Mian of Donghai and repeatedly sent people to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Rong had wished to become acquainted with Xu Mian of Donghai and repeatedly sent people to summon him.

sentences.zh: 勉謂人曰：「王君名高望促，難可輕{敝衣}衣裾。」

translations.literal: Mian said to others: "Master Wang's fame is high but his prospects are short; one can hardly lightly grasp his robe."
translations.idiomatic: Mian said to others, "Master Wang's fame is high but his prospects are short; one can hardly lightly grasp his robe.

sentences.zh: 俄而融及禍。

translations.literal: Before long Rong met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Rong met with disaster.

sentences.zh: 勉由是知名。

translations.literal: Mian became famous on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Mian became famous on this account.

sentences.zh: 太學生會稽魏准，以才學為融所賞；

translations.literal: Wei Zhun of Kuaiji, an Imperial University student, was admired by Rong for his talent and learning;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhun of Kuaiji, an Imperial University student, was admired by Rong for his talent and learning;

sentences.zh: 融欲立子良，准鼓成其事。

translations.literal: Rong wished to establish Ziliang as emperor, and Zhun urged the matter on to success.
translations.idiomatic: Rong wished to establish Ziliang as emperor, and Zhun urged the matter on to success.

sentences.zh: 太學生虞羲、丘國賓竊相謂曰：「竟陵才弱，王中書無斷，敗在眼中矣。」

translations.literal: University students Yu Xi and Qiu Guobin secretly said to each other: "Jingling lacks talent, and Wang the Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary has no resolve—defeat is plain to see."
translations.idiomatic: University students Yu Xi and Qiu Guobin secretly said to each other, "Jingling lacks talent, and Wang the Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary has no resolve—defeat is plain to see.

sentences.zh: 及融誅，召准入舍人省詰問，惶懼而死，舉體皆青，時人以為膽破。

translations.literal: When Rong was executed, Zhun was summoned to the Secretariat of Palace Attendants for questioning; in terror and dread he died, his whole body turning blue-green, and people of the time thought his gall had burst.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong was executed, Zhun was summoned to the Secretariat of Palace Attendants for questioning; in terror and dread he died, his whole body turning blue-green, and people of the time thought his gall had burst.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，魏主至肆州，見道路民有跛、眇者，停駕慰勞，給衣食終身。

translations.literal: On renyin the Wei sovereign reached Sizhou; seeing common people along the road who were lame or blind, he halted his carriage to comfort and reassure them and granted them food and clothing for life.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renyin the Wei emperor reached Sizhou; seeing common people along the road who were lame or blind, he halted his carriage to comfort and reassure them and granted them food and clothing for life.

sentences.zh: 大司馬安定王休執軍士為盜者三人，以徇於軍，將斬之。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Prince Xiu of Anding had seized three soldiers who had been thieves, displayed them before the army, and was about to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Prince Xiu of Anding had seized three soldiers who had been thieves, displayed them before the army, and was about to execute them.

sentences.zh: 魏主行軍遇之，命赦之，休不可，曰：「陛下親御六師，將遠清江表，今始行至此，而小人已為攘盜，不斬之，何以禁奸！」

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign encountered this on march and ordered them pardoned; Xiu would not consent and said: "Your Majesty personally leads the six armies and intends soon to clear the lands south of the Yangtze. We have only just set out and arrived here, yet petty men are already plundering—if we do not execute them, how can we check wrongdoing!"
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor encountered this on march and ordered them pardoned; Xiu would not consent and said, "Your Majesty personally leads the six armies and intends soon to clear the lands south of the Yangtze. We have only just set out and arrived here, yet petty men are already plundering—if we do not execute them, how can we check wrongdoing!

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「誠如卿言。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What you say is indeed true.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What you say is indeed true.

sentences.zh: 然王者之體，時有非常之澤。

translations.literal: Yet the bearing of a true king sometimes includes extraordinary grace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the bearing of a true king sometimes includes extraordinary grace.

sentences.zh: 三人罪雖應死，而因緣遇朕，雖違軍法，可特赦之。」

translations.literal: Though these three men's crime deserves death, by chance they encountered me; though this violates military law, they may be specially pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Though these three men's crime deserves death, by chance they encountered me; though this violates military law, they may be specially pardoned.

sentences.zh: 既而謂司徒馮誕曰：「大司馬執法嚴，諸君不可不慎。」

translations.literal: Then he said to Grand Secretary Feng Yan: "The Grand Marshal enforces the law strictly—you gentlemen must be careful."
translations.idiomatic: Then he said to Grand Secretary Feng Yan, "The Grand Marshal enforces the law strictly—you gentlemen must be careful.

sentences.zh: 於是軍中肅然。

translations.literal: Thereupon the army became orderly and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the army became orderly and solemn.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：「人主之於其國，譬猶一身，視遠如視邇，在境如在庭。

translations.literal: Minister Guang said: "A ruler toward his state is like a body toward itself—he should regard the distant as he regards the near, and regard what is beyond the borders as though it were in his court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Guang said, "A ruler toward his state is like a body toward itself—he should regard the distant as he regards the near, and regard what is beyond the borders as though it were in his court hall.

sentences.zh: 舉賢才以任百官，修政事以利百姓，則封域之內無不得其所矣。

translations.literal: If he raises the worthy and talented to appoint the hundred officers, and rectifies government to benefit the common people, then within his domain none will fail to find their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: If he raises the worthy and talented to appoint the hundred officers, and rectifies government to benefit the common people, then within his domain none will fail to find their proper place.

sentences.zh: 是以先王黈纊塞耳，前旒蔽明，欲其廢耳目之近用，推聰明於四遠也。

translations.literal: Therefore the former kings blocked their ears with cotton and covered their vision with the front pendants, wishing to set aside the immediate use of eyes and ears and extend their clarity and wisdom to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the former kings blocked their ears with cotton and covered their vision with the front pendants, wishing to set aside the immediate use of eyes and ears and extend their clarity and wisdom to the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 彼廢疾者宜養，當命有司均之於境內，今獨施於道路之所遇，則所遺者多矣。

translations.literal: Those maimed and disabled ought to be supported—the government offices should distribute care evenly throughout the realm. To grant it only to those encountered on the road means that many are left out.
translations.idiomatic: Those maimed and disabled ought to be supported—the government offices should distribute care evenly throughout the realm. To grant it only to those encountered on the road means that many are left out.

sentences.zh: 其為仁也，不亦微乎！

translations.literal: Is this not petty as an act of benevolence!
translations.idiomatic: Is this not petty as an act of benevolence!

sentences.zh: 況赦罪人以橈有司之法，尤非人君之體也。

translations.literal: Moreover, pardoning criminals and bending the law of the responsible officials is especially unworthy of a ruler's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, pardoning criminals and bending the law of the responsible officials is especially unworthy of a ruler's bearing.

sentences.zh: 惜也！

translations.literal: What a pity!
translations.idiomatic: What a pity!

sentences.zh: 孝文，魏之賢君，而猶有是乎！

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen was Wei's worthy sovereign, and yet he still did such things!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was Wei's worthy sovereign, and yet he still did such things!

sentences.zh: 戊申，魏主至并州。

translations.literal: On wushen the Wei sovereign reached Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wushen the Wei emperor reached Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 并州刺史王襲，治有聲跡，境內安靜，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: Bingzhou Inspector Wang Xi had a reputation for good governance and kept the region quiet; the emperor commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhou Inspector Wang Xi had a reputation for good governance and kept the region quiet; the emperor commended him.

sentences.zh: 襲教民多立銘置道側，虛稱其美；

translations.literal: Xi instructed the people to erect many steles placed beside the roads, falsely praising his merits;
translations.idiomatic: Xi instructed the people to erect many steles placed beside the roads, falsely praising his merits;

sentences.zh: 帝聞而問之，襲對不以實。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard and questioned him, Xi answered not according to the truth.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard and questioned him, Xi answered not according to the truth.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，降襲號二等。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and reduced Xi's noble rank by two grades.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and reduced Xi's noble rank by two grades.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬子，魏遣兼員外散騎常侍勃海高聰等來聘。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on renzi, Wei sent Acting Supernumerary Palace Attendant Gao Cong of Bohai and others on a diplomatic mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day renzi, Wei sent Acting Supernumerary Palace Attendant Gao Cong of Bohai and others on a diplomatic mission.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，魏主詔車駕所經，傷民秋稼者，畝給谷五斛。

translations.literal: On dingsi the Wei sovereign decreed that wherever the imperial procession passed and damaged the people's autumn crops, five hu of grain would be given per mu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingsi the Wei emperor decreed that wherever the imperial procession passed and damaged the people's autumn crops, five hu of grain would be given per mu.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，追尊文惠太子為文皇帝，廟號世宗。

translations.literal: On xinyou they posthumously honored Crown Prince Wenhui as Emperor Wen, with temple name Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinyou they posthumously honored Crown Prince Wenhui as Emperor Wen, with temple name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 世祖梓宮下渚，帝於端門內奉辭，轀輬車未出端門，亟稱疾還內。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu's coffin was lowered to the ferry, the emperor took farewell inside the Duan Gate; before the hearses had even passed out of the Duan Gate he urgently claimed illness and returned inside.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu's coffin was lowered to the ferry, the emperor took farewell inside the Duan Gate; before the hearses had even passed out of the Duan Gate he urgently claimed illness and returned inside.

sentences.zh: 裁入閣，即於內奏胡伎，鞞鐸之聲，響震內外。

translations.literal: Hardly had he entered the inner quarters when he had barbarian performers play inside; the sound of drums and bells shook inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he entered the inner quarters when he had barbarian performers play inside; the sound of drums and bells shook inside and out.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，葬武皇帝於景安陵，廟號世祖。

translations.literal: On bingyin they buried Emperor Wu at Jing'an Mausoleum, with temple name Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingyin they buried Emperor Wu at Jing'an Mausoleum, with temple name Shizu.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，魏主濟河；

translations.literal: On wuchen the Wei sovereign crossed the river;
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuchen the Wei emperor crossed the river;

sentences.zh: 庚午，至洛陽；

translations.literal: On gengwu he reached Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengwu he reached Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 壬申，詣故太學觀《石經》。

translations.literal: On renshen he went to the former Imperial Academy to view the Stone Classics.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renshen he went to the former Imperial Academy to view the Stone Classics.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，鄧至王像舒彭遣其子舊朝於魏，且請傳位於舊；

translations.literal: On yihai King Su Peng of Dengzhi sent his son Jiu to attend Wei in audience and also requested to transmit the throne to Jiu;
translations.idiomatic: On the day yihai King Su Peng of Dengzhi sent his son Jiu to attend Wei in audience and also requested to transmit the throne to Jiu;

sentences.zh: 魏主許之。

translations.literal: The Wei sovereign granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 魏主自發平城至洛陽，霖雨不止。

translations.literal: From the time the Wei sovereign set out from Pingcheng until he reached Luoyang, the rains did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the Wei emperor set out from Pingcheng until he reached Luoyang, the rains did not cease.

sentences.zh: 丙子，詔諸軍前發。

translations.literal: On bingzi he decreed that all armies advance.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi he decreed that all armies advance.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，帝戎服，執鞭乘馬而出。

translations.literal: On dingchou the emperor donned military garb, took the whip, mounted a horse, and rode out.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou the emperor donned military garb, took the whip, mounted a horse, and rode out.

sentences.zh: 群臣稽顙於馬前。

translations.literal: The ministers prostrated themselves kowtowing before his horse.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers prostrated themselves kowtowing before his horse.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「廟算已定，大軍將進，諸公更欲何雲？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The plans made in the temple are settled and the great army is about to advance—what more do you gentlemen wish to say?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The plans made in the temple are settled and the great army is about to advance—what more do you gentlemen wish to say?

sentences.zh: 尚書李沖等曰：「今者之舉，天下所不願，唯陛下欲之。

translations.literal: Chief Secretary Li Chong and others said: "This campaign we now undertake is what all under Heaven does not wish for—only Your Majesty desires it.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Secretary Li Chong and others said, "This campaign we now undertake is what all under Heaven does not wish for—only Your Majesty desires it.

sentences.zh: 臣不知陛下獨行，竟何之也！

translations.literal: Your servants do not know where Your Majesty intends to go if you advance alone!
translations.idiomatic: Your servants do not know where Your Majesty intends to go if you advance alone!

sentences.zh: 臣等有其意而無其辭，敢以死請！」

translations.literal: We have the intent but not the words—we dare beg with our lives!"
translations.idiomatic: We have the intent but not the words—we dare beg with our lives!

sentences.zh: 帝大怒曰：「吾方經營天下，期於混壹，而卿等儒生，屢疑大計；

translations.literal: The emperor flew into a rage and said: "I am now setting the empire in order, aiming at unification, yet you Confucian scholars repeatedly doubt the great design;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and said, "I am now setting the empire in order, aiming at unification, yet you Confucian scholars repeatedly doubt the great design;

sentences.zh: 斧鉞有常，卿勿復言！」

translations.literal: The axe and halberd have their fixed law—speak no more!"
translations.idiomatic: The axe and halberd have their fixed law—speak no more!

sentences.zh: 策馬將出，於是安定王休等並殷勤泣諫。

translations.literal: He spurred his horse and was about to depart; then Prince Xiu of Anding and the others all earnestly wept and remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: He spurred his horse and was about to depart; then Prince Xiu of Anding and the others all earnestly wept and remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 帝乃諭群臣曰：「今者興發不小，動而無成，何以示後！

translations.literal: The emperor then addressed the ministers: "The undertaking we launch today is no small matter—if we act and achieve nothing, how can we show ourselves to posterity!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then addressed the ministers, "The undertaking we launch today is no small matter—if we act and achieve nothing, how can we show ourselves to posterity!

sentences.zh: 朕世居幽朔，欲南遷中土；

translations.literal: I have long dwelt in the northern wilds and wish to move south to the central lands;
translations.idiomatic: I have long dwelt in the northern wilds and wish to move south to the central lands;

sentences.zh: 苟不南伐，當遷都於此，王公以為何如？

translations.literal: If we do not campaign south, we should move the capital here—what do the princes and dukes think?
